about.heroCopy: Black diamonds were not born of the earth's ordinary pressures. This enigmatic polycrystalline structure carries the weight of a cosmic origin — a depth that absorbs light and redefines what brilliance means.
narrativeBody: Every gem in our collection is meticulously sourced from the earth's deep metamorphic zones, ensuring the internal density of each stone is as pure as the depths it came from.
We do not chase sparkle. We preserve weight and worth. BlackDiamond was founded to bring the world's most serious black diamonds to collectors who truly understand what they represent.
Every transaction is backed by gemological reporting, provenance documentation, and a curatorial perspective built over fifteen years in the field.
about.manifesto: Light passes through almost everything. But black diamonds consume it. In a world that worships sparkle, we worship weight and worth — the irreducible presence of matter that has endured a billion years to arrive in your hands.

education.title: The Alchemy of Darkness
education.intro: Black diamonds are a geological anomaly — opaque, polycrystalline, forged from extreme pressure, time, and mystery.
originBody: Unlike conventional diamonds that crystallize deep within the earth's mantle, the origin story of the black diamond remains a subject of debate.
Its porous structure and unusual traces have inspired both terrestrial and extraterrestrial hypotheses.

properties.title: Exceptional Durability
properties.body: The polycrystalline structure gives many black diamonds outstanding resistance to cleaving.

properties.title: Internal Voids
properties.body: Internal porosity creates the density and signature texture unique to black diamonds.

properties.title: True Black
properties.body: Graphite and mineral inclusions create the distinctive, deep black identity.

education.originQuote: Black diamonds are the only diamond on earth with no connection to kimberlite — the volcanic pipes that carry diamonds from the mantle to the surface.
education.originEvidenceBody: Infrared spectroscopy reveals trace amounts of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons within black diamonds — the fundamental building blocks of stars.
education.rarityCardBody: Black diamonds are found only in the Central African Republic and Brazil — never in the same deposits as conventional diamonds.
education.rawBody: In its natural state, a black diamond may resemble a piece of coal — formless, rough, and bearing the marks of a violent formation history.
education.cutBody: Once polished, black diamonds reveal a metallic luster unlike that of any colorless gem.
education.caratTitle: Find the Right Look for You
education.caratBody: Black diamonds command attention not through sparkle, but through weight and character.

regions.name: Brazil — The Capital of Carbonado
regions.body: Brazilian carbonado is the largest known source of natural black diamonds. Found in alluvial deposits unconnected to any kimberlite pipe, these gems possess a denser polycrystalline body and more concentrated graphite inclusions, producing an intense, light-absorbing black.

regions.name: Central African Republic
regions.body: Gems from Central Africa exhibit higher surface porosity and a distinctive range of luster, from matte to metallic. Their alluvial distribution pattern aligns strongly with impact-origin theory, forming an origin story unlike any other gemstone on earth.

education.gradingIntro: Unlike colorless diamonds graded on the 4Cs, black diamonds are evaluated through a distinct framework built on opacity, structure, and surface character.

gradingCriteria.title: Surface Luster
gradingCriteria.body: Ranging from matte to diamond-like to metallic, a true metallic luster is the rarest and most highly valued in the collector's market.

gradingCriteria.title: Inclusion Density
gradingCriteria.body: The distribution of graphite and hematite inclusions determines the consistency of the black. An even, dense distribution is prized over mottling or translucent patches.

gradingCriteria.title: Structural Integrity
gradingCriteria.body: Unlike single-crystal diamonds, black diamonds are judged by the cohesion of their polycrystalline body — the absence of visible separated grain boundaries under magnification.

gradingCriteria.title: Surface Character
gradingCriteria.body: This records the visibility of microscopic porous structures. Top-grade stones show minimal surface porosity under 10x magnification and reflect maximum light off their facets.

education.cuttingIntro: Cutting a black diamond is fundamentally more complex than cutting a colorless gem. Its polycrystalline structure demands an entirely different approach.

cuttingSteps.title: Structural Mapping
cuttingSteps.body: Before any blade touches the stone, our gemologists map the polycrystalline grain boundaries using polarized light. Cutting across a grain boundary can send fractures propagating through the entire stone.

cuttingSteps.title: Laser Shaping
cuttingSteps.body: Initial shaping is done with laser rather than mechanical sawing. This precision reduces thermal stress and the risk of fracturing common to polycrystalline material.

cuttingSteps.title: Facet Design
cuttingSteps.body: Unlike colorless gems, black diamonds are cut to maximize character and surface luster — not light return. Every decision on form is purely aesthetic and architectural.

cuttingSteps.title: Metallic Polish
cuttingSteps.body: Specialized steel plates charged with diamond powder polish each facet to a flawless metallic sheen. The process takes three to four times longer than polishing a colorless diamond of equal size.
